351.frame: R8395 p.1 = Add MS 4200 f. 98 (Barrière to Prince of Condé, London 15 Sept 1654 NS)
351.saw: One page: about 8 English lines in clear, then about 13 lines of French text interrupted by numeric cipher, two-digit groups separated by points with accent/bar marks over them (e.g. 45 45 81 15 48 ...) and a few French clear words (quil veuille se deffaire de, raison, aussi la, je crois pourtant quil fera, plustost a cause des); one struck-out run; no decipherment written above the numbers.
351.note: R8398 p.1 = f. 101, Condé to Barrière 18 June 1655 NS: clear English with one 2-line run of two-digit groups after 'Concerning' (7 66 a 50 38 ...), so a very short ciphertext; not the named frame. Image is a .jpeg (IMG_R8395_I38829_P.jpeg), not P<n>.jpg.

360.saw: p.1: German instruction for Otto Henrich, Marquis de Caretto, 1630s; calligraphic heading then ~25 lines of mixed code: 3-digit numbers (155 186 ...) plus Latin-letter signs, many circled or boxed, no decipherment. p.7: upside-down block of symbol cipher (Greek/Latin-like glyphs) in about 6 short blocks plus ~7 lines lower down, with German interlinear words ('hundert tausent', 'vor funffundzwanzig', 'Zehr' ...) written between them. p.9: about 25 lines of dense symbol cipher (negative scan) with a few Latin words, no decipherment.
360.note: Images are PNG; decode_fetch.py misses them (TH_..._P1.png).

58.saw: One narrow slip, text running sideways: about 9 lines of numeric cipher, 2-3 digit groups separated by points (238.157.13.180 ...), with a few English words written between (e.g. 'sophistry', 'protons', 'earnestly') and circled numbers (1)(2)(3); no full decipherment.

156.frame: R1126 p.1 (I5703) of 6 pages; R1127 p.1 (I5709) 6 Mar 1518 fragment
156.saw: R1126 p.1: Italian letter (labelled 1517) opening in clear for ~7 lines, then about 16 lines of two-tier sign cipher (small letter-like strokes with superscript marks) to the foot; no decipherment. R1127 p.1: damaged leaf dated 6 Mar 1518 with clear Italian and two short runs of the same signs (about 3 lines in total).

157.saw: Leaf dated 9 Mar 1519 (Caprile, Eger): top-left block of 8 lines of two-tier sign cipher (about 25 signs per line), then a clear Italian explanatory letter of 10 lines saying he writes in cipher because his adversary intercepted his letters; no decipherment.

158.saw: Leaf dated 25 Jul 1520 (Cistarelli): p.1 clear Italian full page with scattered marks only; p.2 about 17 lines of continuous numeric cipher (2-digit groups run together, e.g. 25 86 70 95 ...) with clear Italian at the foot and in the right-hand leaf; no decipherment.

193.frame: R2285 p.1 (I16203) = Clairambault 325 f. 84 (copy, Memoires du regne de Francois I, 5 Jan 1526)
193.saw: Clear French letter of Bayard to Montmorency with one passage of symbol cipher: 3 lines of mixed glyphs (Greek-like letters, nulls and crosses) in the middle of the clear text, margin note in the same hand; clear text around it; no decipherment written over the signs.
193.note: p.2 not viewed. A later copy, not the original.

13.frame: fr. 15564 f. 151 (slip on the right of Gallica view 164, ark btv1b9064027v)
13.saw: A small slip with folio number 151 at top right, dated 'ce xxvj Juin' at lower right with the initials 'MR': 6 lines of French clear text with runs of symbol cipher (Greek/Latin-like glyphs) interleaved between clear words; no decipherment on it.
13.note: The slip sits at the right of a two-leaf view (canvas 164), so the canvas number is not the folio.

277.frame: fr. 3993 f. 148 = canvas 161 (continues on f. 148v/149 = canvas 162; ark btv1b9059229n)
277.saw: Letter headed 'Monsieur de Villeroy', French, with about 4 lines of mixed digit and symbol cipher in the lower third of the recto and several more cipher runs on the next page (two blocks of 6-8 lines on canvas 162, 1595 date at foot); clear text between, no decipherment written on the page.
277.note: canvas = folio + 13 here (canvas 151 = f. 137, canvas 163 = f. 150).

417.saw: Single sheet headed 'Sire!' with about 17 lines of pure numeric cipher, 3-4 digit groups separated by points (1970.981.2345.158 ...), some with superscript letters, closing initials; ink show-through from the verso; no decipherment on the sheet. 421.saw: Sheet headed 'Sire!' with about 17 lines of numeric cipher, 3-4 digit groups separated by points (951.1145.1520.1702 ...), a closing number 1484 and flourish; no decipherment on the page. 435.frame: APP 279a gallery images 0479-0481 viewed, none matched 279a/480a
435.saw: The gallery has 500 numbered images (1_335_0_0_279a_NNNN.jpg, no unit labels on the page). Images 0479, 0480 and 0481 are clear Polish letters from Lukow dated 1773 (pages 1, 2, 3 of one correspondence), not the French 279a/479 or the 2-page 'letters not deciphered' 480a described in the AGAD inventory (APP335.xml: 279a/480a, 1782, 'akta luzne, s. 2', pol.). No cipher seen on those three.
435.note: Image numbers do not equal unit numbers (inventory has 509+ units incl. 480a-480j, 480j alone is 62 pp.); the 480a scan was not located, so nothing was seen of it.

438.frame: WBC edition 428430, DjVu page 1 (7 DjVu files 039-045 in the zip; letter 'N: 10', folio 31, addressed to Szembek)
438.saw: Polish letter of the 1690s-1700s with about 8 lines of numeric cipher in the body: two-digit groups separated by points (52.22.46.55.22.10 ...), with plain letters written above the groups as an interlinear decipherment in a heavier ink ('ze mpod zamosciem odiechal ...'). So a gloss is present on this page. Only page 1 viewed; pages 2-7 not opened.
438.note: Title in WBC: 'List nominata Inflant do Jana Sebastiana Szembeka'. DjVu viewer loads in the frame URL above; zip of the DjVu at https://www.wbc.poznan.pl/Content/428430/download/ (2.6 MB).
